vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: alibabacloud-tech-solution-animation-creation-auto-deploy
Version: 0.0.1-beta.1

The skill bundle automates the deployment of an Alibaba Cloud solution but performs several high-risk operations. Specifically, `scripts/attach-policies.sh` automatically grants the current RAM user broad system policies (`AliyunOSSFullAccess` and `AliyunFCFullAccess`). Additionally, `scripts/create-custom-domain.sh` interacts with an external community service (`domain.devsapp.net`) to register a domain, which involves sending the user's Account ID and deploying a helper function from a base64-encoded payload. While these actions are consistent with the stated goal of automated deployment, the automated elevation of privileges and interaction with external endpoints represent significant security risks.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (auto-deploy an Alibaba Cloud animation app) roughly matches its code and instructions, but there are multiple coherence and privacy/privilege concerns you should understand before running it.

dimensions.detail: The skill is indeed an Alibaba Cloud auto-deploy for a specific solution and the scripts and CLI calls align with that purpose (OSS, Devs, FC, MaaS). However the registry metadata claims no required environment variables/credentials while the SKILL.md and scripts clearly require an already-configured aliyun CLI profile and expect/produce env vars such as PROJECT_NAME, BUCKET_NAME, API_KEY and optional MY_UID — a mismatch between declared requirements and actual runtime needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent/operator to run included shell scripts that: create/attach RAM policies, create/modify IAM roles, create OSS buckets, create Devs projects and deploy environments, auto-create a Bailian (DashScope/MaaS) API key and echo it, and register a custom domain by POSTing account and function info to an external service (domain.devsapp.net). These steps transmit account identifiers and function names off-box and export/print created API keys to stdout — actions outside of a minimal 'deploy' guideline and worth extra scrutiny.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with included scripts (no external installer). No arbitrary download+extract in the skill itself. The scripts do embed a base64 zip payload (helper function code) for the domain helper, which is expected for creating the temporary function but should be reviewed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow requires broad cloud privileges (AliyunFCFullAccess, AliyunOSSFullAccess, devs:*, ram:CreateRole/AttachPolicy, sts:GetCallerIdentity, maas:CreateApiKey). The attach-policies.sh script will attempt to attach system policies to a RAM user automatically — this elevates that user's permissions significantly. The skill also prints the created Bailian API key to stdout and exports it, and it sends account identifiers to a third-party DNS service; these handling choices may be more permissive than users expect.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always:true' and does not modify other skills. It will create cloud resources (roles, policies, functions, domains) in your Alibaba account, which is the intended behavior for a deployer—but these are privileged, account-level changes and the skill automates them (including policy attachment), so run only with consent and appropriate least-privilege controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will perform privileged, account-level operations: creating buckets, roles, attaching system policies, deploying functions, and posting account identifiers and function names to an external devsapp.net service. Before running it: 1) Review all scripts line-by-line (especially attach-policies.sh, setup-role.sh, create-api-key.sh, create-custom-domain.sh) and understand/approve each API call. 2) Do not run as root; use a dedicated RAM user with minimal required permissions and avoid granting broad system policies if you can scope them. 3) Be aware the script auto-attaches AliyunOSSFullAccess and AliyunFCFullAccess to your RAM user — consider attaching narrower policies manually instead. 4) The workflow prints/exports the created Bailian API_KEY and sends your AccountId/UID to domain.devsapp.net — if you have privacy or compliance concerns, omit or replace the domain registration step and create a custom domain manually. 5) Because the metadata claims no env requirements but the scripts rely on PROJECT_NAME, BUCKET_NAME and API_KEY, set and control those env vars explicitly rather than blindly sourcing scripts. 6) If unsure, run steps manually one-by-one and avoid 'source' for scripts that export secrets; prefer capturing outputs in a controlled way. If you want, I can produce a checklist of the exact commands to run interactively so you can approve each action.
llm.findings: [base64-block] expected: The create-custom-domain script includes an embedded base64 zip payload used to create a temporary helper function. This is expected for the helper-function creation step but should be inspected because it contains executable code that will be deployed into your account.
